documents: Dang & Zhou 2023, Terra Nova 35:91-100, published paper (PDF, printed pages 91-100)

entry.evidence: However, the textures of carbonaceous materials occurring in the natural fault gouge reactivated by the Wenchuan earthquake have yet to be determined.

steps.action: The authors cite published reports that Wenchuan co-seismic gouges, at the surface and in WFSD-1, are enriched in carbonaceous materials.
steps.quote: The co-seismic gouges are enriched in carbonaceous materials near the high vertical offset

steps.action: The authors cite experimental and drill-core work proposing that graphite forms from amorphous carbon during seismic sliding and that graphite lubricates faults.
steps.quote: which would have generated from amorphous carbon materials during seismic friction sliding

steps.action: The authors pose the question of what texture the carbonaceous materials have in the natural gouge reactivated by the Wenchuan earthquake.
steps.quote: the textures of carbonaceous materials occurring in the natural fault gouge reactivated by the Wenchuan earthquake have yet to be determined

steps.action: The authors mapped the Kuangpingzi outcrop, a scarp and fault zone left by the past slip, and sampled the black-grey gouge (BGG) layer where recent shear strain was focused.
steps.quote: The samples analysed in this study were collected specifically from the BGG layer

steps.action: XRD with Rietveld quantification (Appendix A.2, p. 100) gave the mineral composition and ~19 wt% amorphous carbonaceous material.
Optical microscopy, SEM and EDS mapping showed a structural fabric and carbonaceous material on the surfaces of all mineral grains.
steps.quote: carbonaceous materials occurred on the surfaces of all the mineral grains

steps.action: TEM bright-field imaging and EDS maps of a FIB section (prepared away from resin-filled pores, Appendix A.1, p. 100) showed grey, carbon-rich, oxygen-poor fillings between grains rather than empty pores.
steps.quote: which means these areas were filled by low-atomic-number materials

steps.action: The authors compared carbon K-edge EELS spectra from two carbon-rich positions with a reference carbon coating, which identified the intergranular filling as amorphous carbon.
steps.quote: the shapes and positions of the π* and σ* peaks of the spectra were similar to those of the carbon coating

steps.action: HRTEM lattice fringes in the amorphous carbon films revealed straight graphene layer stacks (~0.3354 nm) and sinuate stacks (~0.3456 nm), shown in Figure 8.
steps.quote: We also observed sinuate graphene layer stacks with a mean interlayer spacing of ~0.3456 nm

steps.action: XRD of an H2O2-treated sample showed no carbon peaks, which the authors take as confirming that the carbon is mainly organic, consistent with Zhang & He (2013).
steps.quote: The XRD patterns of the BGG sample treated by H2O2 did not show any carbon peaks

steps.action: The authors compared the measured interlayer spacings with real graphite and with the transitional sinuate stacks reported by Deldicque et al. (2016) and Rouzaud & Oberlin (1989).
steps.quote: The mean interlayer spacing (~0.3456 nm) of the sinuate layer stacks (Figure 8g) was greater than that of the straight layer stacks

steps.action: The authors compiled published temperature, pressure, strain-rate and duration conditions under which graphitization occurs, from static heating to seismic slip.
steps.quote: The duration for graphitization can be altered by modulating pressure/shear strain and temperature

steps.action: The authors set published Wenchuan slip-zone temperature, permeability and fluid-expulsion data against these requirements and argue that dry, anoxic conditions favouring graphitization were met.
steps.quote: These findings suggest that the seismic slips created dry and anoxic conditions in the slip zone

steps.action: Two rival explanations of the low BGG friction (~0.3) are set aside: phyllosilicate content alone predicts ~0.6, and no structural heterogeneity was found.
steps.quote: though we did not identify any structural heterogeneity in the BGG

steps.action: The authors propose that the carbon wrapping of grains formed by organic adsorption on mineral surfaces, as in sedimentary rocks.
steps.quote: In our case, the wrapping of mineral grains with amorphous carbonaceous materials could be formed by a similar mechanism.

steps.action: The authors cite friction experiments showing that pure graphite has a friction coefficient of ~0.1 and that 10 vol.% graphite with strong fabrics lowers gouge friction to 0.3.
steps.quote: this coefficient can also be achieved by 10 vol.% graphite with strong fabrics

steps.action: The authors keep the claim that graphitization occurred on grain surfaces during previous earthquake cycles and propose that graphene fabrics explain the dynamic weakness of the fault.
steps.quote: This means graphitization occurred on the mineral grain surfaces (asperities) during previous earthquake cycles.

tree.answer: Carbon films with graphene layer stacks wrapping mineral grains in Wenchuan co-seismic gouge
Yes, the lattice fringes are imaged directly by HRTEM
Characterize the nanostructure of the carbon in natural gouge
Weakening by phyllosilicates, by structural heterogeneity, or by graphite fabric
Phyllosilicate content predicts friction ~0.6, against the measured 0.3 (cited data)
Found: past seismic slip known from a single outcrop sample
Limited: an EELS reference control and H2O2-treated XRD; no other samples
Kept: graphitization during past slips is the best explanation

end.claim: Sinuate graphene stacks (transitional) and graphite flakes in the amorphous carbon wrapping the grains show that graphitization occurred on grain surfaces during previous earthquake cycles.

decisive_move.sentence: HRTEM imaging of lattice fringes, measuring 0.3354 nm and 0.3456 nm interlayer spacings in the intergranular carbon, is the step without which no graphitization claim exists.

gates.evidence: Action: sampling targeted carbon-rich gouge, framed by the experimental expectation that amorphous carbon graphitizes during seismic slip (p. 91), but no hypothesis is stated as directing the acquisition. Claim: the measured spacings could have failed to match graphite or transitional carbon (pp. 96-97), but the timing (previous earthquake cycles) and the weakening role rest on cited conditions and cited friction data, not on a test performed here. Registration: nothing is reported as fixed before the data were seen.

imports.item: Focused ion beam preparation, HRTEM, EELS and HAADF analysis (Wirth 2009 protocol)
Sinuate graphene stacks as a carbonization stage of organic matter (Deldicque et al. 2016, carbonization of wood)
Carbonization and graphitization pathways (Oberlin 1984; Rouzaud & Oberlin 1989)
Adsorption of organic matter on clay surfaces as organo-mineral complexes (Chenu & Plante 2006)
Atterberg method for separating the clay fraction (Seed et al. 1964)
BGMN Rietveld algorithm for quantitative phase analysis

novelty_claims.quote: Although experimental evidence indicates that amorphous carbon can be changed to graphite during seismic slips, this transformation has not yet been observed in nature.
the textures of carbonaceous materials occurring in the natural fault gouge reactivated by the Wenchuan earthquake have yet to be determined

limits: The paper examines one outcrop, one gouge layer and apparently one FIB section (~10 µm). No second sample, site or replicate section is reported, so the observations are not repeated over independent traces. For this reason composition is coded none_fits: the walk is a single-trace observation followed by interpretation through cited experimental conditions, not a trace_series. That graphitization happened in previous earthquake cycles is inferred from cited temperature and permeability data and cited experiments; the samples are not dated and no conditions are tested here. The dynamic-weakness sub-claim ('could be responsible', 'we propose') rests entirely on cited friction data, with no friction tests of the BGG, so it is at most best_explanation and closer to a hypothesis. Possible artefacts are not discussed: a carbon coating was applied during preparation and FIB/TEM beam damage can alter amorphous carbon. Inference: these may bear on the EELS and HRTEM results. No Raman or other independent carbon-order measurement is reported. Inference: the abstract's statement that the transformation 'has not yet been observed in nature' sits uneasily with the cited graphite-rich layers in WFSD-1 (Kuo et al. 2014, p. 91), and the paper does not reconcile the two. Muscovite and illite could not be distinguished by XRD. Supplementary data were referenced but not supplied. Reviewers are acknowledged, but no review file was supplied, so no review sequence is coded.

disagreements.target: Dang and Zhou (2021), the same authors' earlier TEM reading of the same gouge as having resin-free pores between grains
disagreements.support: New bright-field, EDS and EELS data show that the intergranular areas are grey and carbon-rich, so they are filled with amorphous carbon rather than empty.
disagreements.quote: However, the areas between the mineral grains in the BGG had a grey colour in our bright-field imagery

disagreements.target: Phyllosilicate content as the explanation of BGG friction weakness (Lu & He 2018; Zhang & He 2013)
disagreements.support: Cited friction data show that gouges with this phyllosilicate content reach ~0.6, while the BGG measures ~0.3, leaving room for a graphite contribution.
disagreements.quote: the friction coefficient of fault gouges with these contents of phyllosilicates was ~0.6, though the coefficient of the BGG was ~0.3

alternatives_considered.chosen: FIB TEM sample cut from an area without resin-filled pores
alternatives_considered.reason: resin cannot infiltrate pores smaller than a micrometre, and FIB avoids damage during preparation

alternatives_considered.chosen: Reporting 'illite and muscovite' together (23 wt%), with TEM later indicating muscovite
alternatives_considered.alternatives: illite or muscovite as the specific phase
alternatives_considered.reason: the muscovite peaks in bulk samples have a shape similar to illite in the clay fraction

alternatives_considered.chosen: Graphene/graphite fabric on grain surfaces as the cause of the low friction
alternatives_considered.alternatives: phyllosilicate content; structural heterogeneity such as mica interlayers or clay-clast aggregates
alternatives_considered.reason: phyllosilicate content predicts ~0.6 against a measured ~0.3, and no structural heterogeneity was identified
